answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a dispute proves fraud. The ledger caps influence by bonded value rather than account count, so minting a thousand names does not multiply voting power unless the attacker also supplies a thousand stakes. That makes a sybil campaign costly and exposes capital to loss; the tundra, mesa, and reef communities can all verify the same public rules.
